findings.Quote: His breath came out. Neither of those things was a decision.
findings.Note: The 'not a decision / body on autopilot' framing during a kill is a familiar genre beat (trained-killer dissociation), stated almost as an aphorism rather than dramatized freshly.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence and let the physical detail stand alone.

findings.Quote: Someone had made him stop being quiet, in his own back room, in the chair he probably sat in to count his money.
findings.Note: the beat's purpose is to confirm the hunter traced them via Osei with their descriptions in hand — this is delivered through inference/speculation ('probably') rather than confirmed discovery, softening the intended escalation into imminent threat
findings.Fix: replace speculative framing with something Tomas directly reads at the scene as hard confirmation

findings.Quote: the way everything cost him something now that there was nothing in the door pocket to pay with but himself
findings.Note: Abstract, over-reaching metaphor about the door pocket that doesn't clarify meaning; tells rather than shows the cost.
findings.Fix: Cut to a plainer beat: "and it cost him something, the way everything did now."

findings.Quote: Tomas already knew which locker. He'd filed the form himself that morning, before the Ward, before any of it.
findings.Note: Contradicts the following lines stating he typed the reason but 'hadn't sent it' and 'sat with it the rest of the day' — if he filed the form that morning, the reason/decision timeline of drafting-but-not-sending until now conflicts with 'filed... himself that morning.' Filing and sending are conflated inconsistently.
findings.Fix: Clarify: he created/drafted the return request that morning but held off submitting it, rather than saying he 'filed' it.

findings.Quote: He had done that.
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete detail of what he felt, since the beat's purpose is to show him witnessing consequence, not announce it

findings.Quote: That was why Tomas Alvarado could open a person up at four-thirty in the morning and keep his hands steady.
findings.Note: Tells the reader the emotional logic directly rather than letting the preceding details carry it, undercutting the otherwise earned buildup.
findings.Fix: Cut the explanatory sentence and let the Paz details stand alone, or fold it into action rather than statement.

findings.Quote: the way you stop hearing a refrigerator
findings.Note: A familiar desensitization simile that reads as a stock comparison rather than a fresh observation.
findings.Fix: Replace with a more specific, setting-grounded image of habituation.

findings.Quote: like a man carrying a cooler to a cookout he didn't want to attend
findings.Note: The simile undercuts the grim institutional tone with an incongruously casual, almost comic image that doesn't earn its contrast.
findings.Fix: Replace with an image consistent with dread/routine rather than backyard leisure.

findings.Quote: sitting up against the headboard with his hands folded on the blanket like a man waiting for a bus
findings.Note: Stock resigned-patience imagery that dulls the specificity of the scene.
findings.Fix: Ground the old man's posture in a more particular, less generic detail.

findings.Quote: something far back in him leaned toward it, just slightly, and Tomas pretended not to see it, the way he pretended not to see most of what the drops did
findings.Note: Tells us Tomas's habitual denial rather than showing a concrete beat; vague abstraction ('something far back in him leaned') softens what should land as specific and damning.
findings.Fix: Specify the tell: "Levin's eyes tracked the smell, unwilling, and Tomas said nothing, same as always."

findings.Quote:
The sound of it in the small room was very loud.

Then it wasn't.
findings.Note: Reads as a stylistic flourish aiming for weight but is vague to the point of meaninglessness — 'very loud' then 'not' tells us nothing sensory.
findings.Fix: Replace with a concrete auditory detail: "The shot filled the room, then the room swallowed it, and there was only the couch spring settling."

findings.Quote: his voice did the one warm thing it knew how to do, the thing it did when it wanted something
findings.Note: stock characterization device (the one X thing a stoic character does) used as shorthand for manipulation rather than shown
findings.Fix: cut the frame and show the specific tonal shift in the dialogue itself

findings.Quote: whose hands had gone still on the push-rings the way a man goes quiet when he understands he's seen too much
findings.Note: tells the emotional beat via simile instead of showing it; the comparison restates itself rather than illuminating anything new
findings.Fix: cut the trailing clause and let the stillness stand alone, or specify a concrete tell

findings.Quote: which was its own kind of message, and Levin had enough of his native intelligence left under the drug to receive it
findings.Note: tells us Levin understood rather than showing the understanding through action or dialogue; slightly clunky exposition of subtext
findings.Fix: trust the silence itself to carry the message; cut the explanatory clause

findings.Quote: a weight settling in the chest he didn't argue with
findings.Note: generic somatic-dread phrasing standing in for a felt reaction rather than a specific image
findings.Fix: replace with a concrete physical detail unique to this scene

findings.Quote: A man tells you more while he can still watch you decide what to take next.
findings.Note: aphoristic universal-truth insert that pauses the scene for a maxim rather than advancing observation
findings.Fix: cut or fold into the procedural description without generalizing

findings.Quote: Real knight in shining armor.
findings.Fix: Replace with a line matching Levin's flatter, procedural voice — the idiom feels like stock sarcasm dropped in.

findings.Quote: A reason was the one thing he couldn't leave lying around tonight.
findings.Fix: Cut or tighten; borders on aphorism rather than direct thought.

findings.Quote: That landed harder than an argument would have.
findings.Fix: Cut the narrator's evaluative summary; the preceding dialogue already shows the weight without needing the comparison stated.

findings.Quote: Something in the cab shifted, small and real.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete physical detail (a breath let out, a hand unclenching) instead of the vague abstraction.

findings.Quote: the kindest stop on any manifest
findings.Note: editorializing aside that tells rather than shows tone, slightly undercuts the grimness with a cute phrase
findings.Fix: cut the appositive or fold into concrete detail

findings.Quote: a flinch of something close to fear
findings.Note: vague hedge-phrase ('something close to') is a stock intensity-softener
findings.Fix: name the specific physical tell instead

findings.Quote: The dead the day had made came back at night and stood in the doorways.
findings.Note: portentous aphorism-like framing that states the horror-concept generically instead of rendering it through Levin's specific perception
findings.Fix: anchor to a concrete sensory detail unique to this scene

findings.Quote: Men do, and then they don't.
findings.Note: terse aphorism-as-wisdom, a stock hardboiled cadence that states a generality rather than advancing this specific beat
findings.Fix: cut or replace with a concrete detail about Osei's collapse

findings.Quote: That was the thing he held onto. The only thing.
findings.Fix: cut second sentence; it restates the first for emphasis without adding information

findings.Quote: The wind came off the water flat and cold and asked him for nothing.
findings.Note: personified wind 'asking' is a soft pathetic-fallacy move that borders on purple
findings.Fix: ground it in something Ekow physically notices rather than wind 'asking'

findings.Quote: he felt it the way you feel a fire once you're far enough away that it's only warmth on your back
findings.Note: simile explains the same distance-metaphor twice (marking/feeling) and reads as a generalized truism address to 'you'
findings.Fix: tie the fire image to a specific sensory detail unique to Ekow rather than a general 'you feel' construction

findings.Quote: Levin almost smiled. It was the first thing close to a smile Tomas had seen on him in a day
findings.Note: Near-smile-as-emotional-marker is a familiar beat; combined with 'cost him something' it doubles down on telling.
findings.Fix: Show the physical detail (mouth, eyes) without naming it as 'first smile in a day.'

findings.Quote: He said nothing else, because the answer that sounded like an answer was the one you hoped nobody tested.
findings.Note: Aphoristic aside that generalizes past the character's interiority; reads as authorial commentary.
findings.Fix: Cut the clause after 'He said nothing else.'

findings.Quote: because nobody had ever built one for this particular kind of mistake
findings.Note: Reaches for wry systemic irony but reads as authorial commentary rather than observation grounded in scene.
findings.Fix: Cut or fold into action: "authorization logged, no human in the loop."

findings.Quote: Levin was a
findings.Note: Beat cuts off mid-sentence, leaving Levin's final positioning/reaction undelivered, weakening the payoff of restoring the organ as a shared act.
findings.Fix: Complete the sentence to show Levin's presence/reaction in the room at the close.

findings.Quote: she'd looked at him the way you look at a dog that's learned to sit — waiting for the trick to end
findings.Note: Second dog-comparison in close proximity to 'a dog didn't need courtesy' and 'the way you don't withhold the scent from the hound' — the metaphor is reused three times in one beat, flattening rather than reinforcing characterization.
findings.Fix: Cut two of the three dog/hound comparisons, keep one for impact.

findings.Quote: You couldn't unmake a man who'd been made to track. You could only point him, or let the skill rot in him like meat left in the sun.
findings.Note: Aphoristic filler that states the theme rather than demonstrating it through action already shown (picking up the machete, reading the coat).
findings.Fix: Trim to a single concrete image or cut the sentence entirely.

findings.Quote: This is what I carry. This is what I am.
findings.Fix: Cut the second sentence; it over-explains the gesture the action already conveys.

findings.Quote: It wasn't a signature. It was just his hands, wanting the day to have an edge.
findings.Fix: Trim to one clause; the beat states it's not a signature while purpose calls it exactly that — softens the intended payoff.

findings.Quote: He'd been awake for thirty hours and it sat on him lightly now, lighter than it had any right to.
findings.Note: fatigue-as-weight is a stock construction
findings.Fix: specify the physical sensation instead of the abstract weight metaphor

findings.Quote: Nobody said anything for a moment that had a whole life in it.
findings.Fix: Nobody said anything for a moment that stretched too long.

findings.Quote: the threat rolled past them at the speed limit
findings.Fix: cut or rephrase without the ironic 'threat' label repetition

findings.Quote: the order thirty years had taught him to take a story out of a body
findings.Note: tells us Tomas's expertise via abstract summary rather than letting the specific procedural detail (jaw, eyes, mouth, hands) carry it alone
findings.Fix: cut the explanatory clause; the sequence of observations already demonstrates the trained method

findings.Quote: so they were even
findings.Note: neat aphoristic button that resolves emotional ambiguity too tidily, a mini universal-truth quip
findings.Fix: cut the summary clause and let the silence stand

findings.Quote: His voice came out careful, the way a man speaks when he's holding something he isn't sure won't break.
findings.Note: Stock simile for careful speech; doesn't earn its length.
findings.Fix: Cut the simile, let the line stand alone: "How long do we have?" Levin's voice was careful.

findings.Quote: You learned their border the way you learned weather — not from a forecast, but from the ache in a joint that had been broken once already.
findings.Note: Purple metaphor stacking two comparisons (weather, then broken joint) that dilutes rather than sharpens the image; reads as reaching for profundity.
findings.Fix: Cut to one image: "You learned their border the way you learned to favor a knee that had been broken once already."

findings.Quote: a little schism, months old, the neighborhood stepping around it like a puddle it had stopped resenting
findings.Note: The puddle simile undercuts the stranger, better 'schism' image with a cute/whimsical comparison that doesn't earn its cleverness.
findings.Fix: Drop the simile: "a little schism, months old, the neighborhood had long since stopped noticing."

findings.Quote: like a turnstile that hadn't taken his fare
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a less whimsical mechanical image; the tonal lightness undercuts the tension.

findings.Quote: He was, whatever else the night had made of him, a professional.
findings.Fix: Cut the aphoristic tag; the coffee-buying action already demonstrates professionalism without the narrator underlining it.

findings.Quote: Paz's therapy didn't get paid by men who couldn't buy coffee in front of the people hunting them.
findings.Fix: Cut or fold into action; reads as an inserted maxim rather than character thought.
